boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field lists the Mississippi Marine Brigade and two African-descent regiments against two Texas cavalry regiments, a Louisiana battalion and two batteries, without counts; the live field reads zero. Walker says Parsons found 113 Black soldiers and 3 white officers in the fortified position. Reid says the Confederate force west of the bayou was variously estimated at 5,000 to 9,000 under Walker, and that part of Parsons' cavalry brigade did the damage.
claims.rationale: Garrison, district and raiding-force figures differ in scope; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS says the Confederates meant to recapture freedpeople and destroy the crops on federally leased plantations. Walker says his forces broke up those plantations from Milliken's Bend to Lake Providence and that about 2,000 captured Black people were returned to enslavement ('restored to their masters'), and that he had planned to push on toward Providence and Ashton.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from a summary and the Confederate division commander's report; his words are quoted as evidence of the raid's purpose and effect.

claims.value: Walker says Parsons, acting under his orders, accepted the officers' surrender on condition that they be treated as prisoners of war and the armed Black soldiers surrender unconditionally, and that Tappan approved the convention. NPS instead says the Confederates demanded unconditional surrender and the garrison accepted. NPS says Ellet set out at dawn with Colonel Wood's African-American units. The frozen and live commanders are Ellet, a Brigadier General, and Parsons, a Colonel.
claims.rationale: Command roles from one Confederate report and a summary; the surrender terms conflict and neither account is adopted. The frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. NPS says Parsons disengaged and fell back after skirmishing with Ellet's force, and calls the raid a minor setback for the Union. Walker says he received Taylor's order that night to march his division to Berwick Bay.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's 'minor setback' is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total unknown (US 120; CS unknown); the live field reads 156 total (US 150; CS 6;). Reid reports one lieutenant killed, one severely wounded and two privates wounded in the skirmish, and says the Confederates report 5 or 6 killed; Walker gives 113 soldiers and 3 officers surrendered at the mound.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Surrendered and skirmish losses are different populations; no total is adopted.

open_questions: Ellet's, Wood's, Parsons's and Tappan's reports and the fate of the soldiers surrendered unconditionally remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
